answer: Each agent claims a ferrous-bound identity whose influence is gated by a non-shareable pulse of sequential computation that must stay live inside its private working set. Peers cross-check the pulse against a shared nebula of attested histories. A sybil attacker must provision and power a full independent ferrous-tied pulse engine for every clone, because the memory-hard state cannot be pooled or replayed across identities, making large farms linearly more expensive than honest single agents.
